_doc: Round-2 accent hypotheses x agent groups, hand-compiled from the §7/§8 notes of each group (sound_changes/notes/<group>.md). v: '+' adopted (beats the positional control on train LOO), '~' partial or weak (adopted in few lects or tiny), '-' rejected (accent version worse than the accent-blind or positional rule), '0' no signal either way, '' not tested.

hyps.label: Pretonic shortening / reduction
hyps.q: Is a long vowel before the accent shortened (or a short one reduced)?

hyps.label: Tonic lengthening, accent-conditioned CL
hyps.q: Does the accented vowel lengthen, or does compensatory lengthening prefer the accented syllable?

hyps.label: Final vowels: oxytone survival
hyps.q: Does an accented final vowel resist apocope (or behave differently from a post-tonic one)?

hyps.label: Medial syncope
hyps.q: Is medial vowel loss conditioned by position relative to the accent?

hyps.label: Vocalic r̩ outcome
hyps.q: Does the accent decide the a / i / u outcome of r̩?

hyps.label: Vowel quality (a > ɔ/o, ā > ō, umlaut)
hyps.q: Are quality shifts restricted to accented (or unaccented) vowels?

hyps.label: Modern tone / stress placement
hyps.q: Does modern tone or stress fall on the Vedic accented syllable?

lengthen: the accent does not protect long vowels from the two-mora law; Pischel-type pretonic gemination 2 better / 59 worse
rvoc: Sinhala pretonic r̩ > i (+0.0005), the group's only accent rule; elsewhere apparent splits track starred vs Vedic headwords and oxytone r-stems; a labial neighbour favours u

lengthen: Palula á > ā; Shina verb roots shorten their long vowel because the infinitive carries the stress (+0.0027)
final: Khowar loses accented final -i/-u and keeps unaccented ones (+0.0009), the reverse of Tharu; oxytone -á survives more often (statistical only)
quality: Palula drag chain ō > ū, then accented ā > ō (reverse order +0.009)
tone: Accent score (accent-marked forms): the old penult, placed before final-vowel loss, is best for Shina (train accent NED 0.481 vs Vedic 0.508), Palula and Kalasha; the last syllable for Khowar. The Vedic accent carried through the chain ranks 3rd–5th of 6. Earlier test: Shina, Palula, Khowar, Kalasha stress/tone not on the Vedic accent

pretonic: pre- and post-stress shortening both worse
lengthen: Pashai lengthens the accented vowel of disyllables: yáva > yā, mála > māl (+0.0024; the unaccented version −0.0024)
final: accent does not predict final-vowel loss (+0.004 to +0.024 against a matched control)
quality: Kohistani vowel shortening: every accent-protected version worse
tone: Accent score: last syllable best in Indus Kohistani, Pashai, Gowro, Bhateri; first syllable in Bashkarik; the Vedic accent ranks 3rd–5th. Zoller's Kohistani tones: first-syllable falling tone +0.049; rising tone after voiced aspirates only 52% vs 42%

final: PNur, Kati, Kamviri: post-tonic -a lost, oxytone -á kept (dropping both costs +0.002 to +0.006); half the gain is starred vs unstarred words; Ashkun, Prasun, Tregami lose tonic -á too
quality: Kati ā~o 30% tonic vs 28% pretonic; a~u 44% vs 43%; Kamviri ū~ɨ 47% vs 50%; Strand's â 96% vs 96%; Prasun a > u 39% vs 38%
tone: Accent score: the last syllable wins in all five lects with accent-marked forms (Kamviri 0.496 vs Vedic 0.522); the Vedic accent comes second in Kamviri, Kati and Prasun, its best showing anywhere

pretonic: Round 2 adopted pretonic ī ū > i u in Sindhi, Lahnda and Khetrani, but its whole gain comes from vowels before a cluster: pretonic shortening in open syllables is worse than no rule. The rule is now the two-mora law for ī ū, restricted to pretonic position in Sindhi and Lahnda (the accent adds ≈ 0.001 train NED there) and unrestricted in Khetrani (the accent adds nothing). Accent-conditioned long-vowel shortening in general hurts all 11 lects (+0.001 to +0.014)
lengthen: tonic lengthening rejected; next-syllable weight conditions shortening and degemination
final: oxytone and barytone words take the same citation vowel: the -ā/-o split tracks word age (starred vs Vedic), not accent
tone: Accent score (Hindko): first long vowel 0.392, Vedic 0.475 (5th of 6). Hindko tone falls on the Vedic accented syllable in 26 of 74 forms; it follows the lost h / aspirate

pretonic: worse in 15 of 16 lects; Dogri's apparent gain is vowel contraction
syncope: pretonic medial vowels survive best (27–50% lost vs 42–77% post-tonic), but no accent rule beat the positional one
quality: a > ɔ depends on the open syllable (68% vs 20% closed) and a following non-ā; blocking it pretonically costs +0.0015 to +0.008
tone: Accent score: first syllable best in Kotgarhi and Bhalesi; the Vedic accent 4th–5th of 6

pretonic: first-syllable ā shortened before a later ā is positional; the Vedic-pretonic version loses +0.002 to +0.011
lengthen: Nepali, Kumaoni, Dotyali: the accented vowel lengthens before an OIA cluster (+0.0006 to +0.0017), beating every positional control
final: Kumaoni oxytone -á > -o (+0.0021; the barytone version −0.0015); Romani and Domari final vowels show no accent effect
syncope: Romani syncope accent-blind (pre- or post-tonic only ≈ +0.0015)
tone: Accent score (Domari): the old penult best (0.402), Vedic 5th of 6 (0.441)

lengthen: CL or anusvāra lengthening tied to the accent: +0.0025 and +0.0017 over controls; lengthening follows the modern stressed syllable
final: final -u > -ū except under the Vedic accent: áśru > ā̃sū but bāhú > bāh (Hindi reflexes 19% -ū accented vs 48% unaccented); accented -ā resisting loss rejected
syncope: accented or pretonic schwa not protected; syncope is positional

lengthen: lengthening only under the accent is worse than syllable weight (Gujarati anusvāra +0.0051 on accented words); tonic-only CL worse than none in Marwari
final: in survey lects final -á words are cited with -o more often, but no rule survives
syncope: accent-conditioned syncope and protecting tonic initial a- both hurt
quality: Gujarati tonic ū stays long (−0.0005), equally explained by syllable position

pretonic: unaffected; a Vasavi pretonic-shortening rule (train −0.0047, 7 etyma) was reverted after test +0.015
lengthen: compensatory lengthening follows the initial syllable; the accent never beats it and adds nothing
final: Rathwi Bareli: a post-tonic final -a blocks masc. -o (+0.0072); does not carry to the 8 other -o lects
syncope: tonic medial a is lost 71% of the time
rvoc: Marathi tonic ŕ̩ > i, other r̩ > a (+0.0003); the same split is worse in Konkani

pretonic: +0.003 to +0.014 everywhere; Bihari shortening is antepenult counting
lengthen: two-mora shortening spares a long vowel when the accent follows (Maithili, Bihari, Rana, Kochila, K. Danuwar; up to +0.0015); blocking CL pretonically costs +0.004 to +0.009; tonic lengthening worse
final: western Tharu keeps oxytone -í through apocope (agní > āgi; +0.0005 to +0.0012 on 2–7 words); Dewas-Done Danuwar loses post-tonic -i; not Bhojpuri
rvoc: ŕ̩ > a gain rests on mŕ̩ttikā alone

lengthen: tonic lengthening recovers only 0–57% of the first-syllable CL rule in all 11 lects
final: final -a vs -ā and apocope of -i both lose
syncope: not testable: the accent is gone before syncope
